findings.text: Checkpoint overrides must be a full 40-hex sha. At 54d7e83, schemas.py:933 accepts {"commit": <any str>}, and done_record (verbs.py:459) resolves it with s.git.rev_parse, which runs in the main repository (gitrun.py:79, cwd=self.primary), not the goal worktree. {"commit": "HEAD"} therefore resolves to the main checkout's HEAD, usually an integration commit and so an ancestor of the work branch. It passes the is_ancestor check, and the base is recorded as the checkpoint silently. Ref names (main, dev, worktree-only branches) behave the same way. The design's new card text says the literal "HEAD" is refused, which is not true at read_dev. Fix: in validate_submit_output, require SHA.match for the override (message: a checkpoint override is {"commit": "<40-hex sha>"}; omit the key to use the default). Keep the rev_parse and ancestry checks. Card text: 'give {"commit": "<full 40-hex sha>"}; ref names such as HEAD are refused'. Test: HEAD, a branch name and a short sha each get validation, and a full sha is accepted. Optionally apply the same rule to the {"commit"}-only completion at verbs.py:917.

output.summary: Approved. F2 is resolved: §4a matches read_dev. schemas.py:933 lacks a sha check today, SHA (schemas.py:13) can be reused, done_record's rev_parse/ancestry checks stay valid once the input is a full sha, and fill_current_records (verbs.py:917, called only from edit) gets the full-sha rule plus a needed missing-commit refusal. Docs and tests cover the cases. No new material findings.

findings.text: DocsTests.test_prompts_name_full_shas asserts the new wording in fx.ROOT/.zzzops/prompts/{test_design,implement}.md as well as in the templates. Passing would require the goal to edit this repo's .zzzops/prompts, and integrate refuses goal diffs touching policy files, so the goal could not integrate. Assert only plugins/zzzops/zzzops/templates/default/prompts; the .zzzops copies follow through a separate policy change (the design's 4a 'Prompts' bullet should be read as the template copies).

CapabilityTests.test_reclaimed_reopened_correction_keeps_its_capability is vacuous. It uses design, which has no inputs.base in the default graph, and only calls push_dev without re-running base, so the reclaimed card has no lease-side staleness and 'architectural' holds with or without the F1 fix (it passes at 802c016). Rewrite on a node with inputs.base: through_tests, a review_tests changes_requested finding, start test_design (reason reopened), restack_base, abandon, start --reclaim; assert stale_because == ['inputs.base'] and run.capability == 'reasoning' (not routine).

The submitted commands were narrowed. Attempt 1 submitted ["cd .agents && python3 -m unittest test_engine_card_ux test_engine_lifecycle test_engine_schemas test_engine_journeys test_engine_docs", "python3 .agents/prompt_stats.py --check"]; records.test_design.output.commands now has only card_ux and lifecycle. run_tests would skip test_engine_schemas (the design changes schemas.py's checkpoint override check), test_engine_journeys (the design says they must pass unchanged), test_engine_docs and the prompt budget check (the design edits the template prompts). Restore the full attempt-1 list.

Section 2's capability rule does not achieve its stated intent. The design says a reclaimed reopened correction has 'record current, so record_stale is empty' and keeps its own capability, under the rule record_stale == ['inputs.base'] gives routine. On a node with inputs.base (test_design, implement: the case the design calls common), base moving during the reopened attempt makes the record stale too. Live corrections are not part of fp_parts (frontier.py:207-239: reopened requires input_fp == f), so the design's own rec_sb code gives record_stale == ['inputs.base'], and the stated rule yields routine. The verification bullet (line 158) uses design, which has no inputs.base, so it hides this. The rewritten test asserts 'reasoning' and asks implement for an unstated 'no live corrections' condition. State the rule that achieves the intent, e.g. routine only when record_stale == ['inputs.base'] and the node has no live corrections. Also decide the no-lease case: a plain start of a reopened node after base moved is ready/stale with ['inputs.base'], since the frontier checks staleness before corrections, and today it gets routine while carrying corrections. Then align the verification bullet with the test (test_design).

output.summary: Both prior findings resolved (template prompts only; reopened-correction reclaim test now on test_design with inputs.base). Two new material findings: test_design narrowed its submitted commands, dropping schemas/journeys/docs tests and the prompt budget check; and design §2's routine rule (record_stale == ['inputs.base']) contradicts its own stated intent for a reopened correction once base moves, because corrections are not part of fp_parts, so the record is stale on inputs.base too. The test requires an unstated 'no live corrections' condition.

responses.review_tests:1:1: fixed: DocsTests.test_prompts_name_full_shas now loops over fx.TEMPLATES/'prompts' only (plugins/zzzops/zzzops/templates/default/prompts); .zzzops/prompts is no longer read, so implement need not touch policy files. The implementer should edit only the template copies of test_design.md and implement.md (design 4a's '.zzzops/prompts' paths are superseded by this).
responses.review_tests:1:2: fixed: rewritten as outlined, on test_design: through_design, test_design submit, review_tests changes_requested with a finding on test_design, start test_design (asserts reason 'reopened', no stale_because), restack_base, abandon, start --reclaim; asserts reason 'reclaim', stale_because == ['inputs.base'] and run.capability == 'reasoning'. Fails before implementation (KeyError 'stale_because' at the post-reclaim assertion). Decision recorded for implement: in this scenario the test_design record was produced on the old base, so after the restack record_stale is also ['inputs.base'] (a reopened lease's claimed parts equal the record's parts, so the lease-side and record-side sets coincide). A rule keyed only on record_stale == ['inputs.base'] (design section 2) would therefore give 'routine' and fail this test. The implementation must also leave capability unchanged when the node has live corrections (e.g. routine only if record_stale == ['inputs.base'] and no corrections), which matches the design's stated intent that a reclaimed reopened correction keeps the node's own capability. The control test (no corrections, record stale only on base) still expects routine.

spec:
Dogfooding Release 1 (2026-11-01) found several places where workers were misled or under-informed by cards and lease verbs. Fix them together:
1. `abandon` prints the exact restart command (`start G X --as <LABEL> --reclaim`). Plain `start` after an abandon is refused without `--reclaim`, which misled the root agent.
2. A card issued by a reclaim (or any start) whose node's inputs changed since the previous attempt carries `stale_because` and a pointer to what changed (for example the old and new spec blobs or a diff command). Today it says `reason: reclaim` only.
3. A `submit` refused because findings arrived while the worker ran (responses are checked against findings live at submit time) lists those findings with their text and targets, so the worker can answer them without re-reading state.
4. The card's `output_schema` states that a finding reopens its target node. Coordinate with G1000, which adds materiality and non-blocking notes; this item only makes the consequence explicit in whatever form G1000 lands.
5. The task card's top-level `renew` prose and `commands.renew` are merged or clearly labelled, so the runnable command is obvious.
6. CLI_USAGE documents that ZZZOPS_TRACE records network git and gh calls only.
Acceptance: engine tests for 1-3 (abandon output; reclaim card after a spec edit has stale_because; submit refusal lists the new findings); card snapshot tests for 4-5; docs for 6. No extra fetches. Coordinate with G1014, which adds live-lease entries and renew's inputs_changed (reuse its helper for item 2).
title: Make task cards and lease verbs explain restarts, staleness and findings
